source.title: Basic kinetic wealth-exchange models: common features and open problems

accepted.question_text: For the basic homogeneous kinetic wealth-exchange models reviewed in the paper, including the A1, A2, B, C, and D models, can one derive a general analytical stationary solution that explains why the equilibrium wealth distribution is so often well fitted by a Gamma distribution, proves when that Gamma distribution is genuinely stationary, and clarifies the mechanism by which it emerges from the microscopic exchange rules rather than merely appearing as an empirical fit?
accepted.context_brief: General stationary Gamma solution for KWEMs

evidence.quote: The close analogies among the various models are evident, however the existence of a general solution has not been demonstrated, see e.g. Refs. [23, 41].
However, a general demonstration that the Γ-distribution is the stationary solution of KWEMs and an understanding of how it arises is still missing

accepted.question_text: In the generalized homogeneous C-model where each agent's exchanged wealth fraction is constrained to lie between lower and upper bounds equivalent to saving parameters λ and λ′ with λ < λ′ < 1, can one derive a simple analytical formula for the Gamma-distribution shape parameter n as a function of the two saving parameters λ and λ′, rather than determining n only from numerical simulation?
accepted.context_brief: Analytic formula for generalized model parameter

evidence.quote: However, we have not found a simple analytical formula for fitting the dependence of the parameter n on the saving parameters λ and λ′.

accepted.question_text: What is the correct economic interpretation of kinetic wealth-exchange models: how, if at all, can their stochastic exchange rules be connected to genuine economic behavior or microeconomic mechanisms without misleadingly treating the agents as fully informed rational neoclassical agents or reading notions such as saving propensity and risk aversion too literally?

evidence.quote: Finally, we would like to point out that even though KWEMs have been the subject of intensive investigations, their economical interpretation is still an open problem.

Instead, KWEMs provide a description at a coarse grained level, as in the case of many statistical mechanical models, where the connection with the microscopic mechanisms is not visible; however, the equivalence is maintained.
